nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable equality and let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$. Then the reflexive-transitive closure of $r$ is decidable: for all $a, t \in \alpha$ it is decidable whether $t$ is reachable from $a$ in zero or more $r$-steps.
nodes.title: Decidability of the reflexive-transitive closure on a finite type

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable equality and let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$. Then the transitive closure of $r$ is decidable: for all $a, t \in \alpha$ it is decidable whether $t$ is reachable from $a$ in one or more $r$-steps.
nodes.title: Decidability of the transitive closure on a finite type

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable equality, let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$, and let $A \subseteq \alpha$ be a finite set. An element $t \in \alpha$ lies in the finite set of elements reachable from $A$ in one or more $r$-steps (computed as a finite least fixed point) if and only if there is some $a \in A$ such that $(a, t)$ lies in the transitive closure of $r$.
nodes.title: Membership in the set reachable from finitely many sources

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable equality, let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$, and let $a \in \alpha$. An element $t \in \alpha$ lies in the finite set of elements reachable from $a$ in one or more $r$-steps (computed as a finite least fixed point) if and only if $(a, t)$ lies in the transitive closure of $r$.
nodes.title: Membership in the set reachable from a point

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type and let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$. For a finite set $Z \subseteq \alpha$, the set of $r$-successors of $Z$ is the finite set $\mathrm{post}_r(Z) = \{t \in \alpha \mid r(z, t) \text{ for some } z \in Z\}$.
nodes.title: Successors of a finite set

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable equality, let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$, and let $A \subseteq \alpha$ be a finite set. Write $\mathrm{post}_r(Z)$ for the set of $r$-successors of elements of a finite set $Z \subseteq \alpha$, and let $f$ be the step map $f(Z) = \mathrm{post}_r(A) \cup \mathrm{post}_r(Z)$. The finite set of elements reachable from $A$ is $f^{|\alpha|}(\emptyset)$, obtained…
nodes.title: Elements reachable from a finite set of sources

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable equality, let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$, and let $a \in \alpha$. The finite set of elements reachable from $a$ is the finite set of elements reachable from the source set $\{a\}$, that is, the elements reachable from $a$ in one or more $r$-steps.
nodes.title: Elements reachable from a point

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable equality, let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$, and write $\mathrm{post}_r(Z)$ for the set of $r$-successors of elements of a finite set $Z \subseteq \alpha$. For a finite set $A \subseteq \alpha$, the step map sends a finite set $Z \subseteq \alpha$ to $\mathrm{post}_r(A) \cup \mathrm{post}_r(Z)$.
nodes.title: One step of the reachability iteration

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
